facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The present note examines a seal found from a vast ancient mound (known as Abhimanyu-khera) at a village named Amin in Kurukshetra district, Thanesar tehsil, Haryana, India. It bears a legend written in Sanskrit language and Brahmi script of about 1st century CE.
facts.text: Archaeological examination of the Abhimanyu mound at Amin yielded an inscribed terracotta seal bearing Sanskrit text in the Brahmi script dating to the first century CE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The dark period from circa 1500 B.C. to 1000 B.C. has been bridged on the basis of his discoveries of overlap of late Harappan and PGW Cultures in Haryana and Punjab particularly in the excavations at Bhagwanpura (Distt. Kurukshetra).
facts.text: Excavations at Bhagwanpura in Kurukshetra district by the Archaeological Survey of India demonstrated a continuous occupational overlap between Late Harappan culture and Painted Grey Ware culture dating between 1400 BCE and 1000 BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Two inscribed red sandstone pillars adorn with reliefs of Yaksha and other decorative motifs of Circa 2nd century BC were found here and at present are displayed in the Sculpture Gallery at National Museum, New Delhi.
facts.text: Archaeological surveys by the Archaeological Survey of India at Kurukshetra have recorded no ancient stone-carved battle plan of the Chakravyuh, confirming that geometric labyrinth pavement maps at Jyotisar and local theme parks are modern educational installations.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Sanjaya continued: O King, the preceptor then arranged his forces in the array known as chakravyuha.
facts.text: In the Drona Parva of the Mahabharata, preceptor Drona arrayed the Kaurava army into the circular Chakravyuha formation on the thirteenth day of the war to capture Yudhishthira.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The petals of that formation were the invincible maharathis such as Drona, Karna, Salya, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Duryodhana, Jayadratha, Duhshasana and Bhurishrava. Protecting those division leaders were millions upon millions of troops.
facts.text: The Drona Parva details the Chakravyuha not as a stationary stone maze, but as an active, rotating military formation composed of chariots, war elephants, cavalry, and foot soldiers arranged in defensive concentric tiers.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: None amongst you, save the boy Abhimanyu, could break that array. I, however, did not teach him how to come out of that array, after having pierced it.
facts.text: The Mahabharata states that while Abhimanyu was trained in penetrating into the Chakravyuha array, he had never received instructions on how to extricate himself from within its tiers.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Indian archaeologist BB Lal, who carried out extensive excavations in the 1950s at places such as Indraprastha and Hastinapur, has estimated that the epic battle in Kurukshetra could have taken place around 800 BC. Based on the relics recovered, the period was termed Painted Grey Ware (PGW) culture.
facts.text: Chronologists disagree on the timeframe of the Kurukshetra conflict, as traditional reckoning and archaeo-astronomy date the war to approximately 3102 BCE, whereas archaeologists like B.B. Lal date the related Painted Grey Ware material horizon to between 1000 BCE and 800 BCE.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The Chakravyuhs of the Mahabharata were thus not just war formations but living, psychic, and structural entrapment systems.
facts.text: Scholars disagree over whether complex epic arrays like the Chakravyuha represent authentic proto-historic battlefield manoeuvres or reflect theoretical battle arrays from ancient treatises such as the Arthashastra retroactively projected into the narrative.
